 Order

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.120/2023 dated 12.03.2023 registered at Police Station Mohkhed, District Chhindwara for the offence under Sections 366 (a), 376,
376(2N), 376(2J), 376(3) and 313 of IPC and Sections 4(2), 5(J), 5(l), 5(n)/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He further submits that prosecutrix is a consenting party.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Investigation is complete and charge-sheet has been filed.
The applicant is in custody since 13.03.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

According to prosecution,
prosecutrix was aged around 16 years 04 months at the time of the incident. The statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. reveals that she was in consensual relationship with the applicant for almost 7 months.
The scholar register discloses that the date of birth of prosecutrix recorded therein has been amended.
Earlier, it was recorded as 08.04.2007 and later, it was changed to 04.11.2007.
The certificate issued by the school suggests that date of birth is 05.11.2006.
The applicant has filed the birth certificate of prosecutrix as Annexure-A/2, in which her date of birth is mentioned as 25.09.2002.
Thus, it is apparent that the date of birth of prosecutrix has changed from place to place,
In the FIR itself, her age was mentioned as 16 years 04 months.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I find it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Ramkripal Uikey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133408647/
